title: Two patterns of glomerular injury
implementation: Original layered Manim illustration; no raster image generation or tracing

scenes.intent: Explain the three cooperating barrier layers before disease changes
scenes.state: Retain red cells and most albumin; show filtration

scenes.intent: Evolve inflammatory injury into barrier disruption and reduced filtration
scenes.state: Inflammatory cells, local defect, red-cell leakage and some protein leakage

scenes.intent: Place cast formation in the correct downstream location
scenes.state: Red cells collect within a tubular matrix
Return to the labelled healthy barrier

scenes.intent: Show foot-process effacement/slit dysfunction and increasing albumin passage
scenes.state: Flattened processes and heavy protein leakage; no red-cell leakage in this example

scenes.intent: Connect protein loss with the case findings
scenes.state: 5.2 g/day protein, plasma albumin 20 g/L, oedema and hyperlipidaemia

scenes.intent: Compare the two dominant patterns and acknowledge overlap
scenes.state: Matched illustrated states and concise case findings

clinicalDesignDecisions: No universal charge-only explanation of nephrotic proteinuria
Inflammatory mechanism is illustrative rather than a specific unproven diagnosis
Nephritic proteinuria is variable; the 1 g/day value belongs to this case
Cast formation occurs downstream, not in the capillary
Albumin loss and sodium retention both contribute to oedema
Nephritic-to-nephrotic conversion is not implied by the sequence
